doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

title: Long hours and relaxed playing then versus loud music now
summary: A speaker contrasts today's constant tourist playing with the old long nights, few tunes an hour and strolling from camp to camp.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: The music we're playing now in these places, like on the street and everything, it's hardly much pleasure for the musicians or the people that are being entertained because it's constant. Of course they have to do it in modern times, you know what I mean, to turn it over and entertain the tourists and whatnot. During the time these gentlemen were talking about that, we'd be out there and play about in the whole hour. We didn't play no more than about five or six tunes. Is that right, Ruth? Right. Right. And the people would have time to sit down and relax and enjoy themselves, whatever refreshment they had for sale or whatever they brought with them. It was just like a regular country gathering, you know what I mean, even though you were in the city or in the city limits, see. But now everybody's fighting. The musicians don't understand. They're busting their jaws and everything to try to keep everybody happy. The people sitting out there, they, I don't want to see how they can sit in there sometimes. It's so loud. There's no music or nothing. They just go a lot of blasting and whatnot. Yeah. See, but that's the way life is now. But at that time, everybody enjoyed the music, the people that's making the music, and the people that they were making the music for. It was just one big gathering and everybody having plenty of fun. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. See? So I don't know. Imagine in some places in this world there's people still living that way. I don't know. But all the pleasure has been driven out of it now. Oh, we sit up there and we enjoy it because we play from our arts. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. It's a whole lot of treasure to it now. At that time, it was a pleasure. Yeah, because the hours was long. You'd take the hours long. Oh, you'd play from 8 o'clock or 7 o'clock to 3 or 4 o'clock in the morning. Yeah, that's right.
I ain't going to do nothing.
I mean, and those people would think. I ain't going to do it.

People would still be there every time. No, I ain't going to do it. Sure. And you talk about nothing, boy. People used to walk from camp to camp. Sure. Right. You want to be promenading all night. All night and night.

Your friend got campers that you invite you and your wife or some of your friends. Sure. Come to our camp, our band. Now you walk in, just all night, camp and stuff. And them trump and stuff, and Tramon talk like that. Pa, pa, pa, pa, pa, man. You can just give them.
